name: Lorenzo Valla
biography: Renaissance humanist (ca. 1406-57) mentioned as the first to expose the Donation of Constantine as a forgery (1439), on philological grounds -- its Latin could not be eighth-century usage claiming to be fourth-century; Russell notes the irony that he was later made apostolic secretary by Pope Nicholas V. An Epicurean humanist who proved the Donation of Constantine to be a forgery, ridiculed the Vulgate's style, and accused Saint Augustine of heresy; made apostolic secretary by Pope Nicholas V despite (or because of) this unorthodoxy.
central_doctrines: The Donation of Constantine: A forged imperial decree, accepted as authentic until Lorenzo Valla's philological exposure of it as a fabrication in 1439, that served as the legal-historical basis for papal claims to temporal sovereignty in Italy.
